title: streaming-manifest-incrementation-and-rollback-notes-writer
author: Ava Morgan
release_notes: Adds streaming manifest sequence numbers to support incremental downstream consumption; introduces a rollback-notes writer that emits concise changelog fragments when a model profile is reverted.
description:
Motivation: onboarding churn and large onboards produce big manifest diffs that are hard for downstream consumers (release assemblers, telemetry exporters, and compliance hooks) to handle. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: 1) streaming manifest incrementation: manifests published to the registry now carry a compact sequence delta that can be streamed and applied by incremental consumers; 2) rollback-notes-writer: when a model profile version is rolled back (manual or automatic due to stability regressions), a compact changelog fragment is synthesized and persisted to the release-fragments store for downstream release automation and audit.

Scope: model intake pipeline, manifest serializer, release fragment writer, integration tests, and small console UI indicator for pending rollback notes. This is intended to reduce the cost of large diffs, enable incremental downstream syncs, and make rollback events auditable and human-readable.

Key behavior:
- Manifests are versioned with a lightweight monotonically increasing commit sequence (manifest_seq) and a delta payload that contains only top-level profile keys changed (metadata, tags, performance_profile pointers).
- The streaming manifest endpoint (/intake/v1/manifest/stream) supports backpressure-aware chunking and a resumable token tied to manifest_seq.
- Rollbacks trigger a deterministic fragment that lists reverted versions, reason tags (e.g. "perf-regression", "policy-failure"), and a short human summary; fragments are idempotent and signed with registry provenance key.

Implementation notes:
- Added a new manifest sequencer component (manifest/sequencer.go) that assigns manifest_seq and emits a compact index entry. Sequencer persists to the existing manifest-index table with a new schema column (seq bigint) with backfill script included.
- Manifest serializer now produces two artifacts: full manifest blob and compact delta blob (delta contains keys changed and minimal values).
- Rollback-notes-writer listens to the existing profile_revision stream; on receiving a rollback event it runs a deterministic summarizer and writes release fragment JSON to /fragments/release/ directory in object storage.
- Introduced schema migration and a short backfill CLI (tools/migrate_manifest_seq) to incrementally assign seq to historical manifests.
- Added integration tests focusing on: streaming resume semantics, backpressure chunk boundaries, delta correctness for common onboard changes, and rollback fragment contents.

Compatibility and migration:
- Backfill tool must be run in maintenance window for orgs with >100k manifests; it runs in small batches and supports dry-run.
- Consumers that rely on full manifest blobs are unaffected; streaming and deltas are opt-in via Accept headers or query param.
- Rollback fragments are additive and will not change existing release pipelines unless they opt-in to fragments feed.

Risks and mitigations:
- Race between sequencer and concurrent onboarders: sequencer uses optimistic lease + idempotent compare-and-set to avoid collisions.
- Fragment signing depends on KMS availability; fallback mode writes unsigned fragment and emits an alert for operator review.

How to test locally:
- run ./dev/local_registry and ./dev/producer_sim to publish sample manifests; use curl to hit /intake/v1/manifest/stream?resume_token=<seq> to validate resume.
- tools/migrate_manifest_seq --dry-run to validate database changes.

Checklist:
- [x] sequencer implementation + unit tests
- [x] serializer delta output and storage adapter
- [x] rollback-notes-writer + integration tests
- [x] migration tool and docs
- [x] manual QA and load-run on perf-canary (small-scale)
- [x] add console indicator (pending rollback fragments)

See also: ENG-1987 (incremental manifest delivery), SUP-4231 (customer asked for smaller change payloads during onboards).
